pr_title: Add missing barrier to SSIL and SSAO in Very Low quality.

issue_context.title: "Command can't have itself as a dependency" floods console with SSIL enabled and set to Very Low
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions
4.3 dev3 stable.

### Description

After updating my godot project from 4.2.0, this error began flooding the output, both in editor and in-game.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/91162221/148151e8-6042-4aec-9f5b-b52b125feb35)


### System information

Windows 11 - Godot 4.3.0dev3 - Forward+ renderer, using Vulkan - Nvidia GTX 1650, Intel i5 9300H Cpu, 8GB of Ram

### Issue description

After updating my godot project from 4.2.0, this error began flooding the output, both in editor and in-game.
I did not change any setting after updating, and did delete the `.godot` folder and reopened the project in an attempt to rectify the issue.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/91162221/148151e8-6042-4aec-9f5b-b52b125feb35)

```
E 0:00:18:0789   _add_command_to_graph: Command can't have itself as a dependency.
  <C++ Error>    Condition "!resource_has_parent" is true.
  <C++ Source>   servers/rendering/rendering_device_graph.cpp:464 @ _add_command_to_graph()
```

From my testing, this error occurs when `SSIL` is enabled in a WorldEnvironment node, with it's quality set to `Very Low` in project settings.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a world environment node with a new environment
2. Enable `SSIL` in the environment
3. Go to project settings with advanced settings enabled.
4. Under `Environment` in project settings, set the SSIL quality to `Very Low`


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14320456/mrp.zip)
comments: After further testing, this also occurs with SSAO.

This is one of two possibilities:
- The graph validation is erroneous.
- SSIL at low had undefined behavior due to using textures incorrectly (e.g. overlapping slices).

I'll review during the week which of those two that is, but I felt it was worth pointing out we can start running into situations where it's just exposing existing bugs (we had a few of those when the graph was added).
interesting. Looking forward to a fix for this, as Very Low and Low don't really have a visible difference but do have a performance difference.

> 
>     * SSIL at low had undefined behavior due to using textures incorrectly (e.g. overlapping slices).
> 

It was this due to a missing barrier. You can find the code change in the PR although I imagine it'll get merged pretty quickly.

> After further testing, this also occurs with SSAO.

I missed this comment, I can reproduce this as well. Guessing it's a similar issue.

The PR will now fix both SSIL and SSAO. Feel free to point out any more of these issues you run into, it seems the behavior of these algorithms changes quite a bit depending on the quality so the graph might end up exposing some of the undefined behavior it was doing.

review_comments: I don't think we want to be adding a barrier between every pass. Instead, this should likely be the same as SSIL and insert the barrier when `i == 3`
Very low quality only does one pass, so it seemed redundant to add the if. Do you think we should add one for clarity anyways?

Hmmm, I don't know why SSIL and SSAO are different here. AFAIK in both cases we should be inserting the barrier between blur_passes. Also, in both cases, there is only one pass when using very low quality. It seems the issue is that SSIL is inserting a barrier between each of the 4 sub passes, even though they have no dependencies on each other. SSIL should look the same as this one then, I.e. it should add a barrier after every blur_pass and should not add barriers within blur passes

Yeah I approached this PR with the perspective of just fixing the error, but I haven't analyzed what the content does. The main problem behind the error just comes from the lack of a barrier between the different steps (as indicated by the comment headers and the scopes), which are missing in very low quality. Perhaps you'd rather approach this by just deleting these altogether and just insert a barrier after each step?
